title: Divisorial sheaves and the boundary kernel on a normal scheme
statement:
Let $Y$ be an integral Noetherian normal scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-integral-scheme], where Noetherian means admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and normal means that all local rings are integrally closed domains [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let $U\subseteq Y$ be a nonempty open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion]. A prime divisor is a reduced integral closed subscheme whose generic point has local-ring dimension one. A Weil divisor is a finite sum $D=\sum_Z n_Z[Z]$ over prime divisors. Write $k(Y)$ for the function field, the local ring at the generic point [def-sc-function-field]. For a prime divisor $Z$, let $v_Z$ be the normalized valuation of its discrete valuation local ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Define $\mathcal O_Y(D)$ inside the constant sheaf $k(Y)$ by the condition $v_Z(f)+n_Z\geq0$ at every prime divisor meeting the open on which a rational function $f$ is considered, and include the zero section. For a coherent module $M$ [pqf-def-coherent], put $M^\vee=\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_Y}(M,\mathcal O_Y)$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom] and $M^{**}=(M^\vee)^\vee$; reflexive means that evaluation $M\to M^{**}$ is an isomorphism, and rank one means that its generic fibre has dimension one over $k(Y)$.

The sheaf $\mathcal O_Y(D)$ is coherent reflexive of rank one, $\mathcal O_Y(0)=\mathcal O_Y$, and every coherent reflexive rank-one module on $Y$ is isomorphic to some $\mathcal O_Y(D)$. Restriction gives $\mathcal O_Y(D)|_U=\mathcal O_U(D|_U)$, where $D|_U$ retains the prime divisors meeting $U$. Every invertible module on $U$ [def-sc-invertible-module] is the restriction of a coherent reflexive rank-one module on $Y$. If a coherent reflexive rank-one module $F$ on $Y$ restricts to $\mathcal O_U$, then there are integers $m_1,\ldots,m_s$ such that $F\cong\mathcal O_Y(\sum_i m_i[Z_i])$, where $Z_1,\ldots,Z_s$ are precisely the codimension-one irreducible components of $Y\setminus U$. With sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], for any Weil divisors $D,E$ one has $(\mathcal O_Y(D)\otimes\mathcal O_Y(E))^{**}\cong\mathcal O_Y(D+E)$. For any coherent reflexive rank-one $F$, the sheaf $(F\otimes\mathcal O_Y(E))^{**}$ is coherent reflexive of rank one; if $F|_U$ is invertible and $E|_U=0$, its restriction is $F|_U$. All restrictions of duals, double duals and tensor products here are the canonical ones; pullback uses [def-pc-module-pullback].

source.place: Tags 0EBM (lemma-normal-class-group), including its construction from a Weil divisor; 0EBL (lemma-reflexive-normal), the reflexive tensor law; 0BE6 (definition-divisor-invertible-sheaf) and 0BE8 (lemma-normal-c1-injective). Agent-extracted restriction and boundary-kernel formulation, with the convention O(D), not the O(-D) fractional-ideal convention.

proof.text: We work on nonempty affine opens $W=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $Y$. The integral-scheme definition makes $A$ a domain; [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth] makes it Noetherian. The stalk identifications of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field] identify its localizations with the local rings of $Y$ and its fraction field with $K=k(Y)$. Normality of those local rings and [lem-weil-pbc-normal-domain-of-local-normal] make $A$ a normal domain. Height-one points and their local rings are unchanged by passage to an open neighbourhood; the closure of such a point is the corresponding prime divisor. Thus [lem-trf-normal-domain-principal-divisor-kernel] supplies the DVRs, normalized valuations, and finite valuation support of any element of $K^\times$ on $W$.

source.place: Tags 0EBM, lemma-normal-class-group, affine reduction; algebra.tex Tag 031T, lemma-normal-domain-intersection-localizations-height-1

proof.text: For $D=\sum n_Z[Z]$ put $d_{\mathfrak p}=-n_{\overline{\{\mathfrak p\}}}$ on $W$. Apply [lem-per-divisorial-fractional-module-lattices] to these finitely supported integers. Its $I_A(-D)$ consists exactly of the sections prescribed in the statement, and its localization law identifies the sections on every nonempty basic open with the same valuation prescription there. Hence $\mathcal O_Y(D)|_W=\widetilde{I_A(-D)}$. The cited node gives coherence, generic rank one, and module reflexivity; [lem-sfb-affine-reflexive-module-comparison] gives sheaf reflexivity. Coherence is local by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-module-local-on-open-cover]. With $D=0$ the intersection assertion of the lattice node gives $I_A(0)=A$, whence $\mathcal O_Y(0)=\mathcal O_Y$. The empty open has just the zero section.

source.place: Tag 0EBM, lemma-normal-class-group, construction from a divisor, using more-algebra.tex Tag 0AVB, lemma-reflexive-over-normal

proof.text: For an arbitrary open $V\subseteq U$, the nonempty intersections $Z\cap U$ are exactly the prime divisors of $U$; their generic points, local rings and valuations are those on $Y$. Indeed the generic point of an irreducible closed subset belongs to every open meeting it, and taking closure in $Y$ reverses intersection with $U$. Therefore the valuation conditions for $\mathcal O_Y(D)(V)$ and $\mathcal O_U(D|_U)(V)$ are identical. This proves the asserted restriction equality as subsheaves of the same constant field. From the open-set formula in [def-pur-sheaf-hom], restriction of Hom and hence of duals and double duals is canonical. Restriction of tensor products is the canonical isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-tensor-comparison].

source.place: Tag 0EBM, lemma-normal-class-group, invariance of codimension-one data under open restriction; canonical open restriction of sheaf Hom and tensor

proof.text: Let $F$ be coherent reflexive of rank one and fix $F_\eta\cong K$. On $W$ the affine equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction], finite generation [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-affine-sections-finite], and [lem-sfb-affine-reflexive-module-comparison] identify $F|_W$ with a finite reflexive module $M$. By [lem-per-reflexive-height-one-intersection-criterion], $M$ is torsion free and embeds in $M_K=K$, so these embeddings glue to $F\subseteq K$. For each height-one $\mathfrak p$, [lem-sc-dvr-fg-torsionfree-free] makes $M_{\mathfrak p}$ free; its generic rank is one. Write $M_{\mathfrak p}=c_{\mathfrak p}A_{\mathfrak p}$ and $e_{\mathfrak p}=v_{\mathfrak p}(c_{\mathfrak p})$. Choose $0\ne b\in M$ and a common nonzero denominator $a\in A$ for finite generators, so $bA\subseteq M\subseteq a^{-1}A$. If $v_{\mathfrak p}(a)=v_{\mathfrak p}(b)=0$, both bounds localize to $A_{\mathfrak p}$, so $e_{\mathfrak p}=0$. Finite valuation support, Step 1, proves finite support on $W$. A finite affine cover proves global finiteness. At a fixed codimension-one point the lattice $F_\xi\subseteq K$ is intrinsic, so its integer $e_Z$ agrees on all charts.

source.place: Tags 0EBM, lemma-normal-class-group, attaching a divisor class to a reflexive sheaf; 0AVB, more-algebra-lemma-reflexive-over-normal, (3)

proof.text: Set $D=-\sum e_Z[Z]$. At every height-one point the stalk lattices of $F$ and $\mathcal O_Y(D)$ agree: a DVR fractional generator $c$ spans precisely the elements with valuation at least $v(c)$, by the valuation membership criterion in [lem-trf-normal-domain-principal-divisor-kernel]. On $W$, the intersection assertion of [lem-per-reflexive-height-one-intersection-criterion] reconstructs $F(W)$ from these lattices, and [lem-per-divisorial-fractional-module-lattices] reconstructs $\mathcal O_Y(D)(W)$ from the same lattices. Thus these modules are equal inside $K$ on every chart and basic subchart; their identifications glue. This proves $F\cong\mathcal O_Y(D)$ without choosing incompatible local divisor classes.

By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], the nonempty open $U$ is Noetherian; it is integral and normal because its local rings and generic point are inherited from $Y$. If $L$ is invertible on $U$, local frames identify it with $\mathcal O_U$: it is coherent by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth], and evaluation is the identity after these frames. It is reflexive of rank one. Apply Steps 1--5 with $U$ in place of $Y$ to obtain $L\cong\mathcal O_U(D_U)$ with finite $D_U$. Close each prime divisor of $D_U$ in $Y$ and retain its coefficient to form a Weil divisor $D$. Step 2 constructs the required coherent reflexive rank-one $\mathcal O_Y(D)$; Step 3 identifies its restriction with $L$.

source.place: Tags 0BE6, definition-divisor-invertible-sheaf, and 0EBM, lemma-normal-class-group, applied on U and closure of its finitely many prime divisors

proof.text: If $F|_U\cong\mathcal O_U$, choose the generic identification $F_\eta\cong K$ induced by this very trivialization. Then its embedded stalk is $\mathcal O_{Y,\xi}$ for each codimension-one $\xi\in U$, so the construction of Steps 4--5 has $e_Z=0$ for every $Z$ meeting $U$. Every remaining prime divisor lies in $Y\setminus U$ and is an irreducible component of that closed subset: a strictly larger irreducible closed subset containing it would give a prime strictly below its height-one prime, necessarily the generic point of $Y$, which cannot lie in the proper closed complement. There are only finitely many such components: on a finite affine cover their generic primes are among the minimal primes of the ideals cutting out $Y\setminus U$, finite by [lem-sc-finite-minimal-primes-over-ideal]. List the codimension-one components as $Z_1,\ldots,Z_s$, insert zero coefficients for any absent from $D$, and set $m_i=-e_{Z_i}$. Then Step 5 gives exactly the asserted boundary formula.

source.place: Tag 0EBM, lemma-normal-class-group, trivial divisor class on an open; boundary support argument with algebra.tex lemma-Noetherian-finite-minimal-primes

proof.text: Put $T=\mathcal O_Y(D)\otimes\mathcal O_Y(E)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-tensor-product-affine-sections], on an affine chart $W=\operatorname{Spec}A$ its sections are the tensor product $I\otimes_AJ$ of the two finite modules of Step 2, and $T|_W$ is the associated sheaf; finite pure tensors of their generators generate it. Thus $T$ is quasi-coherent of finite type and coherent by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]. Its dual $T^\vee$ and double dual $T^{**}$ are coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-sheaf-hom-coherent], and $T^{**}$ is coherent reflexive by [lem-sfb-coherent-reflexive-hull]. Coherent modules are locally cokernels of maps between finite free modules by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-local-finite-presentation]; hence [lem-weil-pbc-stalk-internal-hom-finite-presentation], applied first to $T$ and then to the coherent $T^\vee$, identifies each stalk $(T^{**})_y$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{Y,y}}(\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{Y,y}}(T_y,\mathcal O_{Y,y}),\mathcal O_{Y,y})$, compatibly with evaluation. For $y\in W$ corresponding to $\mathfrak p$, $T_y=I_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_{A_{\mathfrak p}}J_{\mathfrak p}$; on modules this is the statement that finite Hom commutes with the flat localization, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-hom-finitely-presented] and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat]. At the generic point $T_\eta=K\otimes_KK\cong K$ by multiplication, so $T^{**}$ has generic fibre $K$ and rank one. At a height-one point the stalk lattices are $\pi^{-n_Z(D)}A_{\mathfrak p}$ and $\pi^{-n_Z(E)}A_{\mathfrak p}$; their tensor is free of rank one over the DVR, multiplication sends its generator to $\pi^{-n_Z(D)-n_Z(E)}$, and evaluation identifies a free rank-one module with its double dual. So the exponent is $-n_Z(D)-n_Z(E)$.

source.place: Tag 0EBL, lemma-reflexive-normal, reflexive tensor law; algebra.tex Tag 0583, lemma-hom-from-finitely-presented

proof.text: The generic multiplication $K\otimes_KK\to K$ identifies these stalk lattices with those of $\mathcal O_Y(D+E)$. Both sheaves are coherent reflexive. On every affine chart [lem-sfb-affine-reflexive-module-comparison] and [lem-per-reflexive-height-one-intersection-criterion] reconstruct both modules as the intersection of these same lattices inside $K$. Hence the generic multiplication gives an isomorphism $(\mathcal O_Y(D)\otimes\mathcal O_Y(E))^{**}\cong\mathcal O_Y(D+E)$; the chart maps glue because they are the same generic map. This also covers the field case: the intersection over no height-one primes is all of $K$.

source.place: Tag 0EBL, lemma-reflexive-normal, and 0EBM, lemma-normal-class-group, compatibility with addition

proof.text: For any coherent reflexive rank-one $F$, Step 5 writes $F\cong\mathcal O_Y(D)$, and Steps 8--9 show $(F\otimes\mathcal O_Y(E))^{**}$ coherent reflexive of rank one. If $E|_U=0$, Step 3 gives $\mathcal O_Y(E)|_U=\mathcal O_U$. Restricting tensor and double dual by the canonical comparisons of Step 3 yields $(F|_U\otimes\mathcal O_U)^{**}$. When $F|_U$ is invertible, a local frame identifies the evaluation map to its double dual with the identity of a rank-one free module. Therefore this restriction is canonically $F|_U$, as required.
